_COMMENT_SOURCE: Composition of General Mills Cookie Crisp, per 100 g (recipal.com / USDA-derived): water 0.6, protein 5.2, fat 4.4, carbohydrate 84.5; per 26 g serving sugars 9 g, fiber 1 g, sodium 119 mg -> per 100 g sugars ~34.6, sodium ~458 mg (= ~1.16 g NaCl). STARCH = carbohydrate - sugars. These sum to 95.9 g, so fractions are normalized to 1 (the ~4 % remainder is ash/other, not modeled). MASS fractions of the solids (converted to volume fractions + air by the study).
_COMMENT_GEOMETRY: 50 mm diameter x 10 mm as specified (a 10 mm cube fits: its half-diagonal is ~7 mm).
_COMMENT_GRID: 50 mm footprint -> 70 mm domain (same ~5 mm PML clearance as the earlier 30 mm cylinder); see cookie_butter.json.
_COMMENT_AIR: Composite: 70 % crisp dough with 60 % air (Konstantin, 2026-09-21: air fraction of the crisp WITHOUT its chocolate parts) and a chocolate share of ~30 % (Konstantin, 2026-09-21; read as a VOLUME share of the whole piece), solid (no air), same milk-chocolate recipe as the chocolate layer of the chocolate-waffle (assumption - real chocolate may be darker). The chocolate is placed as DISCRETE 6 mm spheres (Konstantin, 2026-09-21: pieces ~6 mm, spherical), random layout with fixed SEED, minimum gap 0.3 mm, kept clear of the centered foreign object (10 mm keep-out cube) and identical in the baseline and all foreign-object runs. A 10 mm thick slab cannot hold the full 30 % as 6 mm spheres, so as many as fit are placed and the remaining chocolate volume stays in the dough matrix as fine crumbs (effective medium), preserving the total 30 %. CAVEAT: the dough recipe is the sourced General Mills Cookie Crisp nutrition data (cereal as sold); replace it if the product differs.
